name: Pinto Martins International Airport
before:
The airport for Fortaleza, 6 km south of the city centre, and one of the Brazilian airports now run by Fraport Brasil rather than by Infraero, which held it from 1974 until the end of 2017.

The current passenger terminal opened in February 1998 in the southern part of the site and covers 35,000 square metres. The older 1966 terminal on the north side is still in use, as the general aviation terminal for private aircraft, executive charters and air taxi work. A second wave of investment followed in the run up to the 2014 World Cup, when Fortaleza was a host city, covering the terminal, the apron and the parking.

Some facilities are shared with Fortaleza Air Force Base, and the site began as a 1930s runway that became an Allied base in the Second World War, supporting operations across the South Atlantic.

It is named after Euclides Pinto Martins, a Ceará born aviator who in 1922 helped pioneer the air route between New York and Rio de Janeiro.
after:
The airport for Fortaleza, 6 km south of the city centre, and one of the Brazilian airports now run by Fraport Brasil rather than by Infraero, which held it until the end of 2017.

Its current passenger terminal opened in February 1998. Work to extend it for the 2014 World Cup was left unfinished, and Fraport enlarged the terminal between 2018 and 2020. The old passenger terminal now serves general aviation and air taxis.

Fortaleza Air Force Base is next door. In the Second World War the airfield was an Allied air base.

It is named after Euclides Pinto Martins, a Ceará born aviator who in 1922 helped pioneer the air route between New York and Rio de Janeiro.

claims.note: Was 'A second wave of investment followed in the run up to the 2014 World Cup ... covering the terminal, the apron and the parking', which reads as if the work was done. Both Fortaleza papers report the terminal extension stopped in May 2014, when Infraero ended its contract with the CPM Novo Fortaleza consortium, and was still an abandoned building site under a court dispute in April 2018.

claims.claim: an Allied air base in the Second World War
claims.inAfter: In the Second World War the airfield was an Allied air base.
claims.note: Was 'became an Allied base in the Second World War, supporting operations across the South Atlantic'. The 1952 law renamed 'o aeroporto do Cocorote' in Fortaleza as Aeroporto Pinto Martins; Diário do Nordeste's history column says that in the war, when Brazil lent air base areas at Natal and Fortaleza to the Allies, a new unit, Adjacent Field, was set up as the Base Aérea do Cocorote. The South Atlantic role rests on Wikipedia alone.
